title: Normalized compactification reduction models and canonical whole-system maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with integers $O$. On every small pro-etale site use the actual $\ell$-power rings, quotient transitions, ordinary integral and whole-system derived categories, reduction $r_T$, total limit $L_T$ and reduction/limit adjunction of [def-sp-projection-reduction-presentation]. Use the normalized ringed integral operations and open comparisons of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge], the section-model system tensor calculus of [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus], and the varying-ring system pullback, proper image, open extension and their actual adjunctions of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. A pullback/reduction presentation consists of the canonical derived isomorphism $r_X f_R^*\cong f_\bullet^*r_Y$ and its ordinary scalar-extension comparison, fixed on every quotient generator by the actual inverse-image unit and on every whole cochain complex by the reduction representative/counit square. A system tensor/pullback presentation consists of the derived tensor/pullback isomorphism and its ordinary representative comparison, carrying the inverse-image unit of $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the two inverse-image units on every site object. Define $\mathrm{DescentModels}$ to retain the abelian tower and reduction presentations, the normalized ringed models and open comparisons, the system tensor calculus, the tensor/reduction model of [def-sp-projection-reduction-presentation], these pullback/reduction and system tensor/pullback presentations, and an open/scalar isomorphism whose inverse is exactly the open-adjunction mate of the pullback/scalar comparison. These are presentations of the specified maps, not assertions of existence or invertibility of any projection.

For a fixed model, write $r_T,L_T$ and $r_T\dashv L_T$ for its actual reduction, total limit and adjunction, using a normalized-equivalence presentation [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The proper/scalar comparison is the adjunction mate of inverse pullback/scalar comparison. The open/limit comparison is the transpose of open/scalar comparison followed by open extension of the reduction/limit counit; the proper/limit comparison is the corresponding transpose of proper/scalar comparison followed by proper image of the counit. For a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow Z,p:Z\to Y)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], set $P_c=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ and $F_c=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$. Define $a_{c,N}:P_cN\to L_YF_cr_XN$ by $P_c$ of the actual unit $N\to L_Xr_XN$, then proper image of the open/limit comparison, then the proper/limit comparison. Define the pinned reconstruction map $b_{c,N}:r_YP_cN\to F_cr_XN$ as $r_Y(a_{c,N})$ followed by the actual reconstruction counit. Define the system proper projection by the counit mate of tensor/pullback; define the inverse open projection as the open adjunct of unit tensor identity, using that same tensor/pullback comparison. When this inverse open projection is invertible, define the system compactification projection by the proper projection, proper image of its inverse, and the canonical pullback compositor with the compactification equation. No arbitrary comparison isomorphism, completion, or levelwise detection of a whole-system map is introduced.
